> [header 1 lines]
> # Principles
>
> surf aims to be a compliant, minimal and secure browser. These are the rules that follow from that.
>
> 1. **Specification first.** No behaviour exists in code that the specification under [spec/](<https://github.com/beyond10x/surf/tree/main/spec>) [@l25] does not state. A gap is reported, not filled in quietly.
> 2. **Complete means complete.** Work stays marked incomplete until it passes the standard's own tests. Skipped cases are counted and listed by name.
> 3. **Isolation over speed.** A component is a security boundary. A design that needs two components to share memory is refused.
> 4. **No third-party code in what ships.** The Rust standard library and the operating system are allowed. The checks fail if the lock file lists an outside package. One exception is planned: audited cryptographic primitives for TLS.
> 5. **No unsafe code.** Every hand-written crate forbids it. The exceptions are in tests: two counting allocators that measure what a fetch holds and what a parse allocates.
> 6. **Text from the web stays text.** Anything from a page, a server or an address is escaped before it is printed, so a page cannot forge a line of surf's output.
> 7. **A passing test must be able to fail.** Tests are tried against planted defects. A storage that drops every write fails 36 of the 169 scenarios.
> 8. **Small.** A standard is followed for what surf does, not implemented whole.
>
> ## Compliant, minimal, secure[\xe2\x80\x8b](<\#compliant-minimal-secure>) [@l26]
>
> - **Compliant.** Where a web standard covers a behaviour, the specification follows it: the WHATWG HTML, Fetch, URL, DOM, MIME Sniffing and Encoding standards, the W3C CSS specifications, ECMA-262 for script, and RFC 9110 (HTTP) and RFC 8446 (TLS 1.3). The cross-browser test suite for them is web-platform-tests.
> - **Minimal.** A feature is specified only when a step of the plan needs it.
> - **Secure.** Isolation wins over speed and memory.
>
> Compliance is claimed per section of a standard. A section is marked complete only when every requirement in it is specified and the tests the standard's suite has for that section pass (web-platform-tests; test262 for ECMA-262). Everything else is marked incomplete.
